html:
EMA-VFI (Zhang et al., CVPR 2023; large and small, for the middle frame or any time): makes the frame between two video frames from motion and appearance features that inter-frame attention extracts together, for slow motion and higher frame rates. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/MCG-NJU/EMA-VFI at 75b6f6a889e6
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/MCG-NJU/EMA-VFI/blob/75b6f6a889e695df875e103374040d47a4cfac7c/LICENSE ; https://github.com/MCG-NJU/EMA-VFI/blob/75b6f6a889e695df875e103374040d47a4cfac7c/README.md (checkpoints: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16jUa3HkQ85Z5lb5gce1yoaWkP-rdCd0o)
  • Training data: Vimeo-90K (septuplets / triplets for frame interpolation) (README: the fixed-time models train on Vimeo-90K triplets (train.py); the arbitrary-time _t models are evaluated on 4x / 8x benchmarks, their training data is not stated (the paper: Vimeo-90K septuplets).)
  • Options: cuda_graphs = True (speed only), tta = False
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc, ema_warp
  • Variants: ema-vfi, ema-vfi-small, ema-vfi-t, ema-vfi-small-t
  • Outputs: frame
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): ema-vfi 1988x2880 (7.4 GiB peak allocated, 9.1 reserved); ema-vfi-small 3000x4000 (8.9 GiB peak allocated, 11.4 reserved); ema-vfi-t 1988x2880 (7.4 GiB peak allocated, 9.1 reserved); ema-vfi-small-t 3000x4000 (8.9 GiB peak allocated, 11.4 reserved)
  • ema-vfi 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 91 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 91 s (ONNX + engine).
  • ema-vfi-small 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 79 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 68 s (ONNX + engine).
  • ema-vfi-t 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 85 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 92 s (ONNX + engine).
  • ema-vfi-small-t 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 78 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 69 s (ONNX + engine).
  • ema-vfi original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream MultiScaleFlow as Model.inference (no TTA), timestep 0.5, BGR, replicate pad to 32
  • ema-vfi-small original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream MultiScaleFlow as Model.inference (no TTA), timestep 0.5, BGR, replicate pad to 32
  • ema-vfi-t original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream MultiScaleFlow as Model.inference (no TTA), timestep 0.5, BGR, replicate pad to 32
  • ema-vfi-small-t original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream MultiScaleFlow as Model.inference (no TTA), timestep 0.5, BGR, replicate pad to 32
  • ema-vfi load / first call: original 2.69 s / 0.5 s, portable 0.83 s / 0.234 s, kernels 0.81 s / 0.207 s
  • ema-vfi-small load / first call: original 0.36 s / 0.179 s, portable 0.27 s / 0.09 s, kernels 0.56 s / 0.085 s
  • ema-vfi-t load / first call: original 2.77 s / 0.495 s, portable 0.73 s / 0.398 s (480x854), kernels 1.18 s / 0.359 s (480x854)
  • ema-vfi-small-t load / first call: original 1.05 s / 0.175 s, portable 0.28 s / 0.437 s (480x854), kernels 0.56 s / 0.348 s (480x854)
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets for the 180-triplet benchmark. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 5e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.001 and p99 <= 0.005 (absolute error of the output frame).

Limitations

  • CUDA graph replay keeps a private pool and static outputs for the current shape. Use cuda_graphs=false to disable capture or release_graphs() to free the graph.
